steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

title: Converting Sequenced Fuzzy Cognitive Maps to Causal Virtual Worlds with Large Video Generators
summary: The method replaces hand-authored scripting and storyboarding of video scenes with an orchestrated pipeline in which a fuzzy cognitive map encodes causal rules, its feedback dynamics are converted into if-then meta-rules, an LLM writes a script from them, and a large video model renders each scene. It costs nothing locally in model training but depends entirely on paid third-party APIs (Gemini 3.1, Veo 3.1), adds the complexity of authoring and validating an FCM per world, and offers no measurable quality, speed, or cost advantage over direct prompting. Failure modes include an incorrectly specified FCM producing incoherent causal sequences, the LLM mis-translating meta-rules into the script, and the video generator not preserving causal or entity consistency across scenes, none of which are evaluated in the paper.
rationale: The paper demonstrates a single qualitative dolphin-shark example with no benchmarks, ablations, or production-relevant metrics, so there is no validated basis for adoption in a constrained-infrastructure engineering practice.
